title: Direct Security Proof for Unmodified nEHtMp
summary: The modified m-nEHtMp workaround makes additional bad events easier to bound, but a direct security proof for the original nEHtMp construction remains open.

formal_statement.body: Establish a security proof for the original, unmodified $\mathrm{nEHtMp}$ construction by developing techniques strong enough to bound the additional bad events in its analysis. The modified $\mathrm{m\text{-}nEHtMp}$ workaround appends a hash evaluation of the input message $M$ under an extra hash key $h^{\ast}$ to the output tag, thereby adding randomness that makes these bad events easier to bound. The unresolved task is to obtain the proof directly for $\mathrm{nEHtMp}$ without this modification.

scope.domain: Security analysis of the original nEHtMp nonce-based MAC and the modified m-nEHtMp workaround.
parameters: M: input message hashed by the modified workaround
h*: extra hash key used for that hash evaluation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop sufficiently strong bounds for the additional bad events and thereby prove security directly for the unmodified nEHtMp construction.

citations.label: A Modular Approach to the Security Analysis of Two-Permutation Constructions

progress.summary: The source proves security for modified m-nEHtMp, whose extra hash evaluation makes the additional bad events easier to bound. It conjectures that stronger bad-event techniques combined with its new approaches can prove the original construction.
citation_labels: Yu Long Chen et al., A Modular Approach to the Security Analysis of Two-Permutation Constructions
